key_insight: Symbolic regression can discover a compact, physically interpretable skin-friction law for attached airfoil flows directly from inviscid surface data, with corrections for pressure and Mach effects.
engineering_relevance: The resulting formula chain enables fast, low-cost skin-friction drag prediction for subsonic to supersonic attached flows without relying on expensive, grid-sensitive CFD.
method: Use limited Euler surface-solution data plus viscous-flow skin-friction data as training inputs.
Apply symbolic regression to evolve an analytical formula chain with increasing physical corrections.
Interpret terms as streamwise decay, pressure-coefficient correction, and Mach-number/thermodynamic correction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on typical geometries with low average integrated skin-friction drag prediction error and good generalization across freestream conditions and shapes.
watch_item: The approach is intended for attached flows, so performance may degrade in separated-flow regimes or outside the Mach/geometry ranges represented in training data.
paper_title: Skin friction prediction for attached flows based on two-dimensional inviscid solutions
